summary.title: Coding with Character
summary.one_liner: A personal, design-focused tour of monospaced coding fonts with personality (Operator Mono, Comic Code, Vulf Mono, Cascadia Code, IBM Plex Mono and many more), plus a long list of honorable mentions.
takeaways: Monospaced fonts can be designed with personality while keeping fixed-width constraints (e.g. distinguishing 1, I, |, l and 0, O).
Italics are a useful way to make comments and other code parts stand out; several listed fonts have cursive italics inspired by IBM Script and Selectric typefaces.
Notable picks named in the post include Operator Mono, Comic Code, Vulf Mono, Cascadia Code, Dico Code, IBM Plex Mono, Recursive Mono, Input Mono and Monoflow.
Many listed fonts are free or open source (e.g. IBM Plex Mono, Recursive, Input Mono), while others are commercial; the post gives little pricing detail beyond that.
The post explicitly focuses on aesthetics rather than technical features like ligatures or Powerline, and promises a future post on faux-monos.
summary.summary: The author, Doug Wilson, explains his long-standing fondness for monospaced typefaces, tracing it to IBM Selectric typewriters he saw as a child. He then reviews roughly 20 monospaced fonts he finds aesthetically interesting, each with a note on personality and a list of favorite characters, and only includes faces that have both roman and italic styles. The post deliberately skips technical topics such as ligatures and Powerline features. It closes with a long list of honorable mentions and a few "wild" monos, plus a short resources section for technical comparison.
